title: Adversarial fixtures for machinery that consumes model output — semantically wrong, structurally valid
summary: Prep research for the decision 'Require adversarial fixtures for machinery that consumes model output'. PR #1607 (card #3351) added 25 adversarial fixtures to the review pipeline and six found real defects: a juror citing a file not in the diff, `line: 0`/`-12`/`3.7` passing a Number.isFinite check and rendering into the posted comment, `normalizeFindings` coercing a non-array `findings` to [] so a juror that narrated its blockers in prose recorded an ACCEPT, the same for an object-valued `findings`, a forged `citationScope` letting a juror withhold its own finding, and an off-scope downgrade being undone one gate later by `prevention-outstanding`. LOAD-BEARING OBSERVATION: not one was a parse failure — every input was structurally valid JSON, so conventional malformed-input testing would have caught none of them. FINDING 1 — the field's dominant mitigation is the wrong instrument: the structured-output ecosystem (Instructor, Outlines, Pydantic AI, OpenAI structured outputs, GBNF grammars) has converged on constrained decoding, which makes schema-INVALID output impossible by construction and closes none of the six; the practitioner literature already names the residue ('valid structure, meaningless data') and prescribes semantic validators plus verbatim evidence spans, which is precisely what validating a cited file against the net diff is. FINDING 2 — OWASP LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling supplies the correct posture (treat model output as untrusted input) but the wrong threat model: its mitigations target injection sinks (escape SQL/HTML, strip command patterns) because the assumed harm is code execution, whereas the harm here is that the machinery reaches a WRONG VERDICT and acts on it. FINDING 3 — the coercion at we:scripts/lib/jury-core.mjs:445 is Postel's law applied at a trust boundary, whose standing critique is that liberal acceptance destroys the feedback that would correct the sender; with a model as sender there is no feedback loop at all, so the blocker is simply lost. FINDING 4 — LLM golden-set/eval practice is mature but its subject is always the MODEL (does it still answer well); the subject here is the CONSUMER (does the pipeline survive a bad answer), and the two need opposite fixtures — an eval set holds good answers to compare against, an adversarial consumer fixture holds bad answers the pipeline must survive. FINDING 5 (the qualifying test) — mutation testing supplies the only definition of 'adversarial' that neither goes stale nor is gameable: a fixture counts iff some named guard, removed, reddens it. This repo has reached that conclusion twice already — the #3264 tier-1 determinism qualifier ('if the criterion would still pass against a double that returns "" for everything, it is not proving the mechanism') and the shipped we:scripts/operations/mutation-check.mjs, whose three-valued killed/survived/unrun outcome already handles the pattern-typo gaming case. FINDING 6 (placement) — this is not a rival to the existing fidelity gate but the discharge of a documented hole in it: we:scripts/lib/operation-io-fidelity.mjs's debt register permanently exempts `review-pr` and `review-prep` with the stated reason 'declares a `judge` step: the real mechanism needs a model, not a repo'. FINDING 7 — every mechanism a ruling would need is already in the tree: a mechanical consumes-model-output predicate (we:scripts/operations/cli-adapter.mjs:107), a closed step vocabulary making `judge` load-bearing (we:scripts/operations/step-kinds.mjs:36), a fake-model harness (we:scripts/operations/__tests__/helpers/fake-claude.mjs:134), the discrimination proof (mutation-check), the detect-plus-shrinking-allowlist rollout shape, and the register-a-rule shape. FINDING 8 — the hole is live outside the operations tree (we:scripts/review-core-cli.mjs:178 and :273, plus a fail-open at we:scripts/lib/jury-core.mjs:480), and NONE of those has a bug report or a fix in flight, which points at the TRIGGER rather than at the scope. FINDING 9 (correction, recorded because it was nearly shipped) — 'consumes model output' is NOT reliably decidable from a single file: we:scripts/lib/jury-ledger.mjs:252 and we:scripts/lib/verdict-ledger.mjs:430 parse our own JSONL ledger and we:scripts/conveyor/tick-core.mjs:932 parses orchestrator bookkeeping, none of them model output, while the two motivating files take their input from a caller; so the statute states the class by the trust boundary and the GATE works from a DECLARED set, widened by import-graph reachability from the single model-entry seam (we:scripts/lib/judge-spawn.mjs:490) — a source scan for the semantic property was tested against the tree and misses both motivating files while false-positiving on a documented pure leaf, which is the same result we:scripts/lib/operation-io-fidelity.mjs:320-327 already recorded ('gets it wrong in both directions'). FINDING 10 (statute overlap, found by the prep skeptic) — a NEW anchor would duplicate we:docs/agent/platform-decisions.md#agent-convergence-independent-validation clause 2, which already ratifies 'require a test that fails on pre-change behavior for logic fixes' scoped to 'any AI-review/convergence surface in the constellation'; the rule is therefore codified as an AMENDMENT to that clause plus a second qualifier beside the #3264 note, and the genuine gap it fills is the TRIGGER (clause 2 fires on a fix; all six defects had none). Full grounding in we:reports/2026-08-26-adversarial-fixtures-model-output-consumers.md.
